Not compared: the interleaving of the kinds with each other (termData goes through the relay lane's 16 ms buffer, the others at once: remote-relay-push-lanes.ts:80-89 against :139-150), and the `droppable` of termActivity and termSizeOwner (Node sends both never droppable, :139-150; the core's come from its sections, which do not carry a phone frame of their own).
entry: Ran: Node's desktop service (createDesktopService) with its relay leg dialling a scripted relay (relay-capabilities, roster, revoke-client answers), three phones through the relay with the app's own E2EE handshake, `setRemoteLanes`, `termEnsure`, `termWrite`, `termDispose`, `termProfiles` as the phones' calls, and the desktop's own `termEnsure`, `termWrite`, `termDispose`, `remoteAccessRevokeClient`. The PTY is the scripted shell (lib/scripted-pty.mjs through lib/scripted-pty-hooks.mjs): node-pty's ConPTY is not run, and the terminal manager's own code runs on what the shell writes. Not run: a direct (WebRTC) transport; binary relay frames (the relay offers text frames).
framing: Not on a virtual clock, and not needed: every step waits until what it sent reached every phone reading the lane before the next output is written, so the relay buffer holds one chunk at a time; a chunk with nothing waiting is sent at once or after its 16 ms as one frame of its own (terminal-data-buffer.ts:41-58 and :62-87: `flush` sends the joined pending chunks, and the push lane acknowledges each frame as it sends it, remote-relay-push-lanes.ts:83-88, so no high watermark holds any back), and the scripted shell writes each line back in one write over a pipe, one chunk. So one typed line is one termData message on every run, whatever the timing. How the buffer joins chunks that arrive within 16 ms is recorded on a virtual clock in apps/mobile/fixtures/relay-framing and replayed by mixdog-spawn service::relay_buffer.

Each phone's termData, termActivity and termSizeOwner events (what the adapter hands the page) are compared whole with Node's, each in its own order; each termData's envelope `droppable` is that of the relay frame that carried its `process/outputDelta` on the terminal lane feed.
slowPhone: Node's desktop sends every termData to the relay marked `droppable` (remote-relay-push-lanes.ts:85, remote-relay-delivery.ts:131-140) and keeps nothing per phone: a phone that cannot take it is the relay's to skip, with a resync hint, never closed (apps/relay/lib/relay-legs.mjs:304-319 deliverToPhone, relay-transport.mjs:717-733 sendToPhone and admitFrame :308-313; a frame not droppable over a leg's budget cuts the leg). The desktop's memory for it is the relay socket's send buffer, shared by every phone, which one slow phone does not fill: the relay never pauses the desktop's socket for one consumer (relay-legs.mjs:512-516). Recorded: each termData's `droppable`.
